name: Semantic Versioning
purpose: Version-numbering rules (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) that let tools and consumers infer compatibility. A specification, not a release policy: it only means something once your project declares what its public API is.

name: Keep a Changelog
purpose: Convention for human-readable CHANGELOG.md files grouped by Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security. Pairs naturally with SemVer; it rejects raw commit-log dumps as changelogs.

name: Conventional Commits
purpose: Commit-message specification (feat/fix/scope/!) that maps to SemVer and enables automated changelogs and releases. Requires team agreement and a linter to be worth anything.

name: Choose a License
purpose: Short decision guide to common open-source licenses and what happens with none. Guidance, not legal advice; confirm obligations with counsel for commercial or mixed-license projects.

name: SPDX License List
purpose: Canonical short identifiers, names, and license texts used in package metadata and SBOMs. Use SPDX IDs in manifests instead of free-text license names.

name: REUSE Specification
purpose: File-level licensing metadata via SPDX headers and a LICENSES/ directory, plus a linting tool. Makes per-file provenance auditable in mixed-license repositories.

name: Architecture Decision Records
purpose: Practices and templates for recording architectural decisions with context and consequences. Cheap to adopt; value comes from writing them at decision time, not retroactively.

name: Diátaxis
purpose: Documentation framework separating tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation. Useful structure test for docs that mix four different reader needs into one page.

name: Contributor Covenant
purpose: Widely adopted code of conduct with enforcement guidelines. Fill in the reporting contact and review the enforcement section before publishing it.

name: The Twelve-Factor App
purpose: Methodology for portable, operable services: config in the environment, stateless processes, logs as streams. Guidance from the Heroku era; some factors need reinterpretation for serverless and Kubernetes.

name: C4 model
purpose: Hierarchical approach to architecture diagrams: context, container, component, code. Notation- and tool-independent, which helps when diagrams must survive tool changes.
